name: John Oliver Place

location.text: Cades Cove, Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Blount County, Tennessee

dates.altered: NPS: 'A kitchen was added to the present cabin but has since been removed by the National Park Service.'
dates.note: NPS: 'A second cabin, the one that still stands today, was built in the 1820s just a few dozen yards from the original cabin'; Wikipedia's Cades Cove article: 'constructed circa 1822-1823'; the park's Cades Cove Opportunities Plan inventory prints 'Date of Origin ... 1817' for it; the node's exemplar says the 1820s replacing an 1818 cabin. All kept.

refs.title: John Oliver Place (U.S. National Park Service)
refs.note: Owner. 'The John Oliver cabin is the first historic structure on the 11-mile Cades Cove driving loop. It is also the oldest.'

refs.title: Great Smoky Mountains National Park Cades Cove Opportunities Plan Appendix E
refs.note: The park's cultural-resources inventory. Its own words: 'the John Oliver Cabin, is a one-and-a-half-story, single-room, half-dovetail notched log cabin set on fieldstone footings. It has a single-story front and rear porch, with a wood-shingled shed roof supported by three poles set on a half-sawn log floor. The structure has a stone chimney, and a gable roof with wood shake'.

note: The Park Service's inventory description -- single pen, half-dovetail, fieldstone footings, stone chimney, shed-roofed porches front and rear -- is the nearest thing to a survey this cabin has in words; HABS photographed it and wrote nothing. The appalachian-log-house node names it at the same location string and could join this record. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
